Trading Economics data summary, read 08:47 BST (data only)

t 5.3708 UK 10 Year Bond Yield - Summary The UK 10-year gilt yield slipped below 5.35%, the lowest in three weeks, due to renewed appetite for government bonds amid a global equity selloff. At the same time, the latest data showed GDP expanded by 0.1% in August, following a 0.4% increase in July, avoiding forecasts of a contraction. Output also grew 0.7% over the three months to August, marking a fourth consecutive month in which growth exceeded expectations. The resilience of the economy, despite elevated energy costs and borrowing expenses, has drawn attention from Bank of England policymakers and could strengthen the argument for another interest-rate increase next month to contain inflation risks linked to the Iran war. The figures come ahead of Chancellor John Healey’s first budget on October 28. Although stronger activity could prompt an upgrade to the UK’s growth outlook, rising gilt yields and pressure to support households leave the government with limited fiscal flexibility. UK 10 Year Bond Yield - Stats The yield on United Kingdom 10Y Bond Yield eased to 5.34% on October 15, 2026, marking a 0.06 percentage points decrease from the previous session. Over the past month, the yield has remained flat, and it is 0.84 points higher than a year ago, according to over-the-counter interbank yield quotes for this government bond maturity. Historically, the UK 10 Year Bond Yield reached an all time high of 16.09 in November of 1981. UK 10 Year Bond Yield - data, forecasts, historical chart - was last updated on October 15 of 2026.
